clue.text: Broadcast about old lady who's going abroad?

definitions.note: a clause standing for a noun: one who is going abroad

indicators.note: about means one word goes around the other, so the broadcast word wraps the old lady

parts.note: to broadcast a signal is to emit it
an old lady is informally a gran

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a radio programme about an elderly woman heading overseas might be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal. The definition is a clue-style description, 'one who's going abroad', so the question mark flags it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone leaving their homeland to settle in another country is an emigrant.

clue.text: Tent, brand new on the inside

parts.note: a marque is a brand, especially of car

indicators.note: on the inside asks for the middle letter of the word new, its inner part

explanation.surface: A tent that is brand new on the inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brand new' looks like one phrase, but 'brand' is MARQUE and 'on the inside' takes the middle letter of 'new', E.
explanation.definitionFit: A marquee is a large tent used for parties and shows.

clue.text: Wacky Gorgonzola sandwiches

indicators.note: the word sandwiches means the cheese name holds the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: An odd sandwich filled with blue cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Gonzo means bizarre or crazily unconventional, as in gonzo journalism.

clue.text: A large lady off on holiday wants constant food from morning till night

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or awry, so the letters of lady are rearranged

parts.note: a holiday is a break
constant, as in a firm friend, means fast

explanation.surface: A big woman on vacation wants to eat all day long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges LADY to LDAY, giving A + L + LDAY = ALLDAY; 'wants' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafe meal of bacon, eggs and the like served at any hour is called by this name.

clue.text: Tennyson initially scribbled secret lines of verse

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of the poet's name Tennyson
scribbled suggests letters dashed off in a jumble, so the word secret is rearranged

explanation.surface: The poet Tennyson secretly jotted down some verses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' and 'scribbled' do the work; Tennyson is a poet, which makes the verse surface seamless. The anagram gives ERCETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tercets are groups of three lines of poetry, units of verse.

clue.text: Look after architect

definitions.meaning: to bring up or care for a child not your own
Norman ..., the British architect of the Gherkin and Wembley Stadium

explanation.definitionFit: To raise a child in care is one sense; Lord Norman Foster, a famous British designer of buildings, is the other.

clue.text: Identification process used by CIA once to finger criminal

indicators.note: criminal treatment of these letters means they are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: An American spy agency once used a suspect's fingerprints to identify a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used by' is a link; 'criminal' rearranges all fifteen letters of CIA ONCE TO FINGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Software that matches a photographed face to a known person is an identity-checking technique.

clue.text: Aim to tour island, following street musicians

indicators.note: following means the other pieces come after the street abbreviation
to tour means going around, so the word for aim surrounds the island

parts.note: an aim is an end, as in a means to an end
Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile

explanation.surface: Some street performers aim to go on a tour of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to tour' is the container signal, giving EELBAND, and 'following' puts that after the street. 'Aim' looks like a verb but is a noun, an end.
explanation.definitionFit: A group playing oil-drum pans, Caribbean style, is a band of performers.

clue.text: Limit miles covered by old plane, perhaps

parts.note: ex, as in ex-wife, means former or old

indicators.note: covered by means the miles abbreviation sits within the tree

parts.note: the plane is an example of a tree, hence perhaps

explanation.surface: An old aircraft that has covered many miles may be at its limit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' suggests an aircraft, but it is the plane tree; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The extreme is the furthest point, the outer bound of something.

clue.text: Engineer and inventor largely out of control

indicators.note: out of here is read as outside of, so the shortened inventor goes around the word for control
largely means most of the word, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Alexander Graham Bell, inventor of the telephone
to run a business is to control it

explanation.surface: An engineer and inventor have lost control of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' drops the inventor's last letter, and 'out of', read as outside, wraps what is left round the control word. Isambard Kingdom Brunel was the great Victorian engineer.
explanation.definitionFit: Isambard Kingdom Brunel built the Great Western Railway and the Clifton Suspension Bridge, so he is the classic British engineer.

clue.text: Cheese dish, note, served with claret surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly hints that the letters of claret come out unexpectedly rearranged

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A cheese dish arrives with a note and, unexpectedly, a glass of red Bordeaux.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' gives the anagram RACLET, before the note. Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Raclette is a Swiss meal of melted cheese scraped over potatoes.

clue.text: Teacher's responsibility to express disapproval over violent action

parts.note: to tut is to click the tongue in disapproval
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
rage is violent anger or action, as of a storm

explanation.surface: A teacher must voice disapproval of violent behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link. In cricket an over is a set of six balls, written O on scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutorage is the office or charge of a tutor, his or her guardianship of pupils.

clue.text: Freedom from anxiety as judge suppresses false rumour

indicators.note: suppresses means holding down within, so the judge contains the falsehood

parts.note: ref, short for referee, is a sporting judge
a lie is a falsehood, a false story

explanation.surface: Relief comes when a judge quashes an untrue rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suppresses' is the container signal: the judge holds down the falsehood, just as the surface says.
explanation.definitionFit: Relief is the easing of worry, the removal of distress.

clue.text: Take a look round part of castle

indicators.note: round means turned around, so the word for a look is read backwards

parts.note: to peek is to take a quick look

explanation.surface: Have a look around a section of a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns PEEK into the four letters wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: The keep is the central tower, the stronghold, of a medieval fortress.

clue.text: Speak condescendingly to a priest on getting converted

indicators.note: converted means changed in form, so the letters of a priest on are rearranged

explanation.surface: A priest talks down to someone he is converting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting converted' rearranges A PRIEST ON.
explanation.definitionFit: To patronise is to treat someone with an air of superiority.

clue.text: Graduate, with time, pockets such a small amount of earnings?

indicators.note: pockets means holds inside, so the outer pieces enclose the word for such

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate
an age is a long period of time
sic is Latin for thus or so, used in print as such

explanation.surface: A graduate pockets a modest salary over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pockets' is the container signal, with the Latin 'such' inside. The question mark admits the definition is a loose description.
explanation.definitionFit: The basic wage is minimal pay before extras, often a modest sum.

clue.text: Hum at start of Wagner operas is irritating

definitions.note: a verb phrase: the clue's 'is irritating' means 'is annoying'

indicators.note: at start of puts the smell at the front of the operas

parts.note: hum is British slang for a bad smell, and BO is body odour
The Ring is Wagner's four-opera cycle

explanation.surface: A humming noise at the start of a Wagner performance annoys the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hum' looks like a sound, but in British slang it is a bad smell, so BO. Wagner's Ring cycle is four operas.
explanation.definitionFit: Bothering means pestering or annoying someone.

clue.text: Indonesian island has adopted English language

indicators.note: has adopted means taken in, so the island holds the English abbreviation

parts.note: Bali is an island in Indonesia

explanation.surface: An Indonesian island has taken up English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has adopted' is the container signal: the island takes the language abbreviation into its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Bengali is the tongue of Bangladesh and West Bengal.

clue.text: Investigate a kind of therapy after snip goes wrong

indicators.note: after puts the therapy behind the muddled letters
goes wrong signals that the letters of snip are muddled

parts.note: ECT is electroconvulsive therapy

explanation.surface: Someone looks into a course of therapy following a botched operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes wrong' gives the anagram INSP, and 'after' sets the therapy behind it; 'snip' as an operation suits the medical surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect is to examine closely, to look into.

clue.text: Soft wet earth put back in ditch

indicators.note: put back means turned backwards, so the soft and earth pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: P is the music abbreviation for piano, soft
mud is soft wet earth

explanation.surface: Muddy earth is shovelled back into a trench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' reverses P + MUD as a whole. 'Soft wet earth' reads as one phrase but splits as Soft = P and wet earth = MUD; 'ditch' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To dump something is to get rid of it, to discard it.

clue.text: Means to construct model place of pilgrimage? Wrong

parts.note: Mecca is the Muslim holy city of pilgrimage
wrong answers the question with a no, as in 'that's wrong'

explanation.surface: A model kit is offered, then a guess at a holy city is dismissed as wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The question 'place of pilgrimage?' gets the answer 'Wrong', i.e. NO. Meccano is a British construction toy of metal strips and bolts.
explanation.definitionFit: Meccano is a toy kit of metal parts for building small machines and vehicles.

clue.text: Well-liked wine at uncle's place

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
hock is German white wine from the Rhine

explanation.surface: A favourite white wine is served at an uncle's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncle' is old slang for a pawnbroker, so goods at uncle's are pawned.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods pawned are held at the pawnbroker's shop, and the pawnbroker is jokingly called uncle.

clue.text: Captain takes sailor on boat

parts.note: skip, short for skipper, is a captain
jack, as in Jack Tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A ship's captain brings a sailor aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' and 'on' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A skipjack is a sloop-type sailing craft used for oyster dredging.

clue.text: Just no way to get very cold drink

indicators.note: no means without, so the word for way is removed from just

parts.note: ST, short for street, is a way
ice is extremely cold

explanation.surface: There's simply no way to get an ice-cold drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes ST from JUST, leaving JU; 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit juice is a drink squeezed from fruit.

clue.text: Steer vehicle in reverse towards one northern street

indicators.note: in reverse means the word for vehicle is read backwards

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
I is the Roman numeral one
in northern English towns like York, gate means a street

explanation.surface: A driver backs a van towards a northern road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'towards' is a link. Street names such as Stonegate in York use 'gate' for street.
explanation.definitionFit: To navigate a ship or car is to direct its course.

clue.text: Current business area to north of Spanish island

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
biz is informal for business

explanation.surface: Business on a Spanish island is booming in the northern part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link. The definition is adjectival, 'of Spanish island', meaning from Ibiza.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibizan means belonging to Ibiza, a Balearic party island.

clue.text: Strip clubs near West End

parts.note: dives are seedy clubs or bars

indicators.note: End takes the final letter of the word West

explanation.surface: Strip clubs close to London's West End.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs' looks like a card suit, C, but it is DIVES; 'near' is a link. The West End is London's theatre district.
explanation.definitionFit: To divest is to strip someone of something, to deprive.

clue.text: Smell only recalled fruit

parts.note: a tang is a sharp smell or taste

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word for only is read backwards

parts.note: sole means only, as in sole heir

explanation.surface: A smell of fruit is the only thing someone remembers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' reverses SOLE to ELOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangelos are citrus hybrids of tangerine and pomelo.
